newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices again hold with crude, gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices again hold with crude, gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices again mostly held steady Tuesday in thin trade, supported by a stable crude market and still-firmer East Coast city gate gas prices that have prompted some utilities to switch to oil.

"This is a shoulder month and there's no load, but with gas prices moving up, we've seen a couple of utilities sniffing around," said one cash trader, adding there was little weather on the horizon to stir East Coast demand.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was steady to up slightly at $14.25-50 a barrel, with paper sellers looking for higher numbers but few, if any, takers, traders said.
NYH May one percent paper was offered 25 cents higher at $14.75, while June sellers were asking 25-50 cents more at $15.30. Traders said July was offered at $15.60.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour was unchanged at $15.25, while New York high sulphurs also were flat on the day. NYH three percent was still talked on either side of $14, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent edged up slightly to $14.50-75, while three percent held at $13.25-50.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
There was no word on a Florida utility tender for 120,000 or 180,000 barrels of one percent or 1.8 percent for May 12-June 3 delivery. Bids were due Tuesday, May 6.

New York city gate swing gas prices firmed a nickel Tuesday to the low-$2.50s/mmBtu, or $15.94 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, again gained about two cents to the mid-$2.20s/mmBtu, or $14.18 a barrel.
